newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha inches up, end-users sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha inches up, end-users sidelined.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha was slightly firmer on Wednesday as bidders outnumbered sellers, although prices remained near five-month lows, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha for first-half June was assessed at $212.00/213.00 per tonne, compared with quotes around $212.00 in late Tuesday trade.
Earlier on Wednesday, one first-half June cargo was rumoured to have been traded at $213.00.
The half-month spread from first-half June remained flat, while the one-month spread from first-half June onward remained in backwardation.
In the physical naphtha market, end-users largely kept a low profile despite recent declines in Asian naphtha prices, traders said.
A lack of storage space due to sizable domestic stockpiles made it impossible for most petrochemical firms to take advantage of relatively cheap spot naphtha cargoes, they said.
In middle distillates, jet kerosene cargoes were notionally quoted at $1.10 to $1.30 over the mean of Singapore quotes on a cost and freight (C and F) basis amid sluggish demand.
